- which area are you investigating?
  - los angeles police department
- what problem does it have?
  - overpolicing and crime
- which variables will you use?
  - rate of reported overpolicing
  - rate of crime
- what do you expect to find?
  - probably that predpol doesn't reduce overpolicing over time
  - i expect to see that the new program either slightly reduces overpolicing or no change
- what's still missing here?
  - level of measurement: ratio-level rates (e.g., arrests per capita, arrest/reported-crime ratio), aggregated by time period
  - unit of analysis: census tract preferred (matches ACS demographic data granularity), LAPD division as fallback depending on crime/arrest data granularity
  - datasets: [@los-angeles-police-department_2024_crime-data-2010], [@los-angeles-police-department_2024_crime-data-2020], [@los-angeles-police-department_2024_arrest-data-2010], [@los-angeles-police-department_2024_arrest-data-2020], [@u-s-census-bureau_2020_american-community-survey], [@u-s-census-bureau_2024_american-community-survey], [@u-s-census-bureau_2024_tiger-line-shapefiles], [@los-angeles-times_2024_times-neighborhood-boundaries]
